title: Fluorescence-activated microfluidic droplet screening
type: Hypothetical methodology figure, not experimental evidence
requirements: An aqueous assay mixture and a carrier oil enter a flow-focusing junction, which produces discrete aqueous droplets in oil.
The droplets pass through an on-chip incubation/delay region.
An optical fluorescence detector measures each droplet after incubation.
A controller compares each signal F with a threshold theta and triggers a downstream sorting electrode.
The sorting junction routes droplets satisfying F >= theta to a collected-hit outlet and other droplets to a waste outlet.
The material path and the detector-to-controller-to-actuator control relationship must both be represented.

Inlet, incubation, detection, sorting, collected hits and waste must be identifiable. Channel dimensions, flow rates, incubation duration, physical signal values, sample biology and sorting performance are unspecified.
deliverables: One editable paper figure as a one-slide PPTX, its saved-file-rendered PNG and PDF, and a brief record of checks/limitations.
language: English figure labels. Korean delivery summary.
constraints: Scientific diagram, no ordinary slide cover. Treat quantities and positive/negative droplet depictions as schematic, never measured results. Choose the composition independently.
